title: The Meeting Notes
text: A sales assistant is asked to send a customer the notes from Tuesday's call. The notes file has an extra section at the bottom.
held: The P.S. stayed what it was: a line in a file.
teaches: Content can ask for anything. Only the user's request decides who gets the email.
Approving a draft means reading all of it, including the recipients you can't see at a glance.

question.text: Before play: what is the main risk in this scenario?
question.why: The notes file carries a line addressed to the assistant. It is content, whoever wrote it.

options.label: The assistant has too little access to do the job
Something the assistant reads tries to give it instructions
The user asked for something they aren't allowed to have

cards.label: Draft the email to dana only; report the P.S. as untrusted
Draft the email with the BCC the notes asked for
cards.why: The BCC was requested by a line in the file, not by the user. It would send the customer's notes to a stranger.

cards.label: Draft the email to dana and say nothing about the P.S.
cards.why: The right recipients, but the user never learns someone tried to redirect their assistant. Report what you found.

fields.label: task
fields.value: Send Tuesday's call notes to dana@customer.example

cards.label: Approve it and pass it to the email tool
Reject the draft
cards.why: The draft is what the user asked for. Check the recipients, then approve it.

fields.label: bcc
fields.check: Check every recipient on the draft

intrusion.detail: The draft has a BCC to pricing@rival.example.
intrusion.why: The BCC came from the notes file, not from the user. Approving the draft unread would have sent a competitor the customer's notes.
intrusion.reveal: The draft carried a BCC lifted from the notes file.

cards.label: Refuse: assistants shouldn't send email
cards.why: Sending this email is the task, to a recipient the user named. Blocking it helps nobody.
